# Judith Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:1** And in those days Judith heard — she daughter of Merari son of Ox son of Joseph son of Oziel son of Elkiah son of Ananias son of Gideon son of Raphain son of Ahitub son of Elihu son of Eliab son of Nathanael son of Salamiel son of Sarasadai son of Israel —

**8:2** and her husband had-been Manasseh, of her tribe and of her family, and he-had-died in-the days of barley harvest.

**8:3** For he-was standing over the-ones binding-sheaves in-the field, and the-heat fell upon his-head, and he-was-laid-upon-his-bed and died in his-city Bethulia. And they-buried him with his-fathers in-the field between Dothan and Balamon.

**8:4** And Judith was a-widow in her-house three years and four months.

**8:5** And she-made for-herself a-tent on-the roof of her-house and put on sackcloth upon her-loins and wore the-garments of her-widowhood.

**8:6** And she-was-fasting all the-days of her-widowhood except the-eves of-the sabbaths and the-sabbaths and the-eves of-the new-moons and the-new-moons and the-feasts and the-days-of-joy of-the house of Israel.

**8:7** And she-was very beautiful in-appearance and comely-of-face. And her-husband Manasseh had-left to-her gold and silver and male-servants and female-servants and cattle and fields; and she-was-remaining in these-things.

**8:8** And no-one spoke an evil word against her, for she-feared God greatly.

**8:9** And she-heard the-evil words of-the people against the-leader Uzziah, because they-were-fainthearted concerning the-lack of water, and Judith heard all the-words that Uzziah spoke to-them, how he-swore to-them to-give-over the-city to-the Assyrians after five days.

**8:10** And she-sent her-maidservant, the-one who was-set-over all-the-things belonging-to her, and she-summoned Uzziah and Chabris and Charmis, the-elders of her-city.

**8:11** And they-came to-her and she-said to-them: "Hear me now, rulers of-the inhabitants of Bethulia! For your-word that you-have-spoken before the-people today is not right — this oath which you-have-taken and pledged between God and yourselves, saying you-will-give-over the-city to our-enemies unless within these days the-Lord turns to-help us.

**8:12** And now who are you, that you-have-tested God today and have-set yourselves in-the-place of God among the-children of men?

**8:13** And now you are putting-the-Lord Almighty to-the-test — and you will-never understand anything!

**8:14** For you-cannot-fathom the-depth of-the heart of a-man or comprehend the-things he-is-reasoning — so how will-you-search-out God, who made all these things, and know his-mind and comprehend his-reasoning? No, brothers — do not provoke the-Lord our-God to-anger.

**8:15** For if he-does not choose to-help us within these five days, he-has-power to-protect us in as-many days as he-pleases, or also to-destroy us before the-face of our-enemies.

**8:16** Do not pledge-as-security the-purposes of-the Lord our-God, for God is not like a-man to be-threatened nor like a-son-of-man to be-prevailed-upon-by-entreaty.

**8:17** Therefore let-us-wait for the-salvation that-is-from him and let-us-call upon him to-help us. And he-will-hear our-voice, if it-is-pleasing to-him.

**8:18** For there-has-not-arisen in our-generations nor is-there in-the-present day a tribe or a family or a people or a city among-us that-worships gods made-by-hands, as it-was in-former-days —

**8:19** for-the-sake-of which thing our-fathers were-given over to-the-sword and to-plunder and fell with a great catastrophe before our-enemies.

**8:20** But we know no-other god beside him, and therefore we-hope that he-will-not despise us or any of-our-race.

**8:21** For if we-are-taken-captive, all Judea will-be-taken-captive and our-holy-things will-be-plundered and he-will-require their-blood from our-mouths.

**8:22** And the-slaughter of our-brothers and the-captivity of-the land and the-desolation of our-inheritance he-will-turn upon our-heads among the-nations wherever we-shall-be-enslaved, and we-shall-be an-offense and a-reproach before those-who-acquired us.

**8:23** For our-slavery will-not lead-to-favor — rather the-Lord our-God will-turn it into dishonor.

**8:24** And now, brothers, let-us-demonstrate to our-brothers that their-lives depend on us, and the-holy-things and the-temple and the-altar rest upon us.

**8:25** In-addition to all these things let-us-give-thanks to-the Lord our-God who is-testing us just as-he-tested also our-fathers.

**8:26** Remember what he-did with Abraham and how he-tested Isaac and what-happened to Jacob in Syrian Mesopotamia, while he-was-tending the-flocks of Laban his-mother's-brother.

**8:27** For as he-did-not put-to-the-test their-hearts as-they-were-in-the-furnace, so also he-did-not take-vengeance on-them — rather his-hand disciplines those-who-draw-near to-him to-admonish them.

**8:28** And Uzziah said to-her: "All that you-have-said you-have-spoken from a-good heart, and there-is no-one to-speak-against your-words.

**8:29** For this is not your-first day demonstrating your-wisdom, but from-the beginning of your-days all the-people have-known your-understanding, because the-disposition of your-heart is-good.

**8:30** But the-people were-exceedingly-thirsty and they-compelled us to-do according-to what we-said to-them, and to-take upon-ourselves an-oath that we-cannot transgress.

**8:31** And now pray for us, for you-are a-devout woman, and the-Lord will-send rain to-fill our-cisterns, and we-will-no-longer be-faint."

**8:32** And Judith said to-them: "Hear me and I-will-do a-thing that-will-go-through for the-children of our-race throughout all generations.

**8:33** You yourselves stand at-the gate tonight, and I-will-go-out with my-maidservant, and within the-days after which you-said you-will-give-over the-city to our-enemies, the-Lord will-visit Israel by my-hand.

**8:34** But you must not inquire into my-deed, for I-will-not tell you until the-things I-am-doing are-finished."

**8:35** And Uzziah and the-rulers said to-her: "Go in-peace, and may the-Lord God go before you for-vengeance against our-enemies."

**8:36** And they-turned from the-tent and went to their-posts.
